paragraphs.text: Cross-session semantic memory for DeepSeek Harness: indexes session history locally with EmbeddingGe
mma 2 embeddings and recalls relevant past context, injecting it as clearly-framed untrusted context
. No runtime dependencies, no service to run, synthesis opt-in.
# dsh-g-memory
Cross-session **semantic memory** for DeepSeek Harness.

DSH already ships an FTS5 full-text index over session history. That finds sessions
whose *titles* o

r exact tokens match. It cannot answer "what did we decide about the
retry policy three weeks ago".

This plugin adds the missing layer: a local,
semantic index of what happened across your sessions, q

the missing layer: a local,
semantic index of what happened across your sessions, queried on demand.

Retrieval runs entirely on your machine: the only network call is to a **local**
embedding server. O

ptional LLM synthesis is **off unless you name an endpoint**
(see Network and privacy).
## What it remembers
| Source | Kept? | Why |
| `user/message` (human turns) | ✅ | The actual conversation. Runtime injections (`source.kind = plu
gin`, e.g. prompt snapshots and reminders) are filtered out — they are not memory and would otherwis

e dominate the index. |
| `assistant/message` (durable prose) | ✅ | What was concluded, explained or

decided. |
| Streaming fragment events (`chunk` families) | ❌ | 84.6% of all events in a typical lo

g; no independent meaning. |
| `tool/result` — measurements, errors, command output | ✅ | **The most
fact-dense content in the log.** On the development corpus the strings `5.95`, `-0.000033` and `512
token` appeared **zero** times in conversation prose and *only* in tool output. Without these, the

memory can recall "what we discussed" but never "what we measured". |
| `tool/result` — file reads,

blob JSON | ❌ | Re-readable on demand, and they crowd out real memories. |
| `tool/call` — a call th
at **names a file** (`write`, `edit`, …) | ✅ | **The only record of a file's history.** The disk kee
ps the latest state, so what was overwritten or deleted exists nowhere else. Measured on this corpus
: 1,004 such calls holding 2.45 MiB, of which **6.7%** of sampled windows were findable anywhere in
the index and **71% of the calls were findable nowhere** — the memory could not answer "which file d

id we put that in". After indexing them: **97.1%** and **1%**. |
| `tool/call` — shell commands, `ru
n_code` bodies | ❌ | Measured at +4.0 MiB and +6.9 MiB of mostly re-runnable noise. A file write is
a durable artefact; a scratch computation is not. |

Chunks are cut at **sentence boundaries** (800 chars for prose, 1200 for tool
output, 120-char overl

ap). This is not cosmetic: fixed-width cutting separated
values from the labels that explain them, a

nd sentence-aligned cutting is what
lets the retrieval arms complement each other.
## Retrieval
Two arms, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion:

- **vector** — 768-d embeddings from **EmbeddingGemma 2** (the current default:
`embed.model: embedd

inggemma-2`, `embed.url: http://127.0.0.1:11439`),
int8-quantised, cosine over every unit. It wants

a role-specific instruction in
front of the text, which is why `embed.queryPrefix` / `embed.docPrefi

x` exist:
the caller states whether it is embedding a query or a document and the prefix
is applied

once, at the wire. Measured on this corpus (28 labelled cases, 99-way
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- Node.js >= 20 (`toWellFormed`, `AbortSignal.timeout`).
- The **`zstd` CLI on `PATH`**, or `DSH_G_M

EMORY_ZSTD` pointing at one. This is a
hard requirement, not an optimisation: DSH writes session log

s as a sequence of
independently flushed zstd frames, which `node:zlib` refuses, so indexing
cannot

read them without it. Note that stock macOS does **not** ship `zstd`
(`brew install zstd`).
- An Ope

nAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint for building the index and for
every query. `llama-server`
with an embedding model works; see `DSH_G_MEMORY_EMBED_URL`.
### Export shape (why there is no `export default`)

A Host plugin must export `name`, `apply`, and an `inject` list naming every
service it reads. This

package exports exactly those three and **no default**,
for two reasons that are easy to get wrong a
nd invisible when you do:

- The Loader resolves a plugin module as `exports.default ?? exports`, so a
default export discards

every named export — `inject` included.
- Without a declared `inject`, a service is simply absent wh

ile `apply()` runs:
the Loader derives each fiber's start from its declared dependencies. The
plugin

then returns early and the fiber still reports `active`, so the
capability vanishes with nothing lo
gged and nothing failing.

`scripts/test-loader-contract.mjs` drives the real Cordis through both rules, in
both load orders, s

o neither mistake can ship again. Both are documented in
`docs/SECURITY-REVIEW.md`.
## Network and privacy
| What | Where it goes | When |
| Chunk text for embedding | `DSH_G_MEMORY_EMBED_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:11439`) | Every `bu

ild`, and every query |
| Query + top candidates for synthesis | `DSH_G_MEMORY_LLM_URL` | Only if yo

u set that variable |
| The turn's own messages, redacted, for the judge | the chat judge endpoint (
`DSH_G_MEMORY_JUDGE_CHAT_URL`) | On every turn the judge is asked, including a session's first one —
resident cards are offered alongside it rather than instead of it |
Two consequences worth stating plainly:

- **Synthesis is opt-in and has no default endpoint.** With `DSH_G_MEMORY_LLM_URL`
unset there is no

synthesis at all, and the plugin tells you so rather than
guessing at a URL. Nothing about your ses

sions leaves the machine unless you
name a destination for it.
- **Pointing `DSH_G_MEMORY_EMBED_URL`

at a remote host sends it everything.**
The embedding endpoint receives raw, unredacted chunk text

— redaction applies
to the synthesis path only, because that is the path designed to cross a trust
b
oundary. Treat the embedding endpoint as a trust boundary too.

When synthesis *is* configured, the query and the candidate text are redacted
before they are sent (

private keys — a PEM block is kept whole by the chunker so
the `BEGIN`/`END` pair survives, cloud an

d provider tokens including
`sk_live_…`/`rk_live_…`, `NAME=value` assignments for anything named lik

e a secret,
emails, home paths and non-loopback IPs). Redaction is a denylist and therefore incomple

te: the control that matters
is that synthesis does not run unless you asked for it.
